# CraftLogin

> CraftLogin is an open-source OpenID Connect provider for Minecraft Java Edition identities. Websites can add “Sign in with Minecraft” without collecting Minecraft passwords or email addresses.

Use OpenID Connect Authorization Code Flow through a maintained OIDC library. CraftLogin requires a fresh state value and PKCE S256 for every public and confidential client. Register exact callback URIs; wildcards are not allowed. Never expose a confidential client secret to browser code or an AI tool.

## Integration

- [Complete integration context](https://craftlogin.com/llms-full.txt): Protocol requirements, identity claims, implementation rules, and review checklist.
- [Copyable implementation prompt](https://craftlogin.com/#implement-with-ai): One simple prompt for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and similar coding agents.
- [OIDC discovery](https://craftlogin.com/.well-known/openid-configuration): Authoritative issuer metadata and endpoint URLs.
- [OpenAPI](https://craftlogin.com/openapi.yaml): CraftLogin HTTP API reference outside the standard OIDC protocol.
- [Developer Console](https://craftlogin.com/developers): Register public or confidential applications and exact redirect URIs.

## Identity

- Request `openid profile`.
- Use `sub` (the canonical Minecraft UUID) as the stable account key.
- Use `preferred_username` only as a changeable display name.
- `picture` is the current Minecraft avatar URL.
- `acr` and `amr` identify the completed verification method.

## Optional

- Request `offline_access` only when refresh tokens are genuinely required.
- Prefer discovery metadata over hard-coded endpoint paths.
- Do not log codes, tokens, secrets, state, nonce, PKCE verifiers, cookies, or complete callback URLs.
